science_checks.topic: Calorie, specific heat and process conditions
science_checks.reason: Source calorie convention retained; approximately 1000 cal/(kg times Celsius temperature interval) for water is not presented as a universal exact value. Specific heat depends on material/state/process. C=mc and Q=cm times temperature change use a common process, approximately constant c, no phase change and negligible other energy changes/work.
Heat entering a body is positive; release is negative. Released-heat magnitude is distinguished from signed Q. Heating/cooling substitutions and all source equation labels are consistent.

Cup, outer vessel, cork, air gap and lids are retained as prose descriptions of approximate insulation, not an exact zero-leak guarantee. Water/iron heat balance explicitly neglects ambient exchange, calorimeter absorption, work and phase changes. Positive masses and heat capacities put the final temperature strictly between the initial temperatures.

The cooler body's Q1 is positive and the hotter body's Q2 negative, giving Q1+Q2=0 for the stated boundary. The generalized sum includes nonnegligible calorimeter heat; significant external exchange prevents assuming a zero sum for the selected bodies alone.

The complete source c2 numerator/denominator and signs are retained. Positive c2 follows for t1<t<t2, with specific-heat dimensions. Constant-c/no-phase-change/no-reaction assumptions and the warning against uncorrected cup/leak data bound the measurement model.

Source section 2, seven-year-course context and the middle-of-eighteenth-century historical attribution are preserved as source context, not newly validated chronology. No unsupported new historical claim or necessary mathematical erratum identified.

symbolic_reasoning: c1*m1*(t-t1)+c2*m2*(t-t2)=0 gives t=(c1*m1*t1+c2*m2*t2)/(c1*m1+c2*m2). Positive finite capacities and t1<t2 imply t1<t<t2.
Solving the same balance gives c2=c1*m1*(t-t1)/(m2*(t2-t)), positive in that domain and dimensionally a specific heat.
The source convention 1 cal per 1 g of water per 1 Celsius temperature interval scales to 1000 cal/(kg times Celsius temperature interval).
